research_targets.rationale: fMRIPrep is the most widely used fMRI preprocessing pipeline in neuroscience. It has strong citation chains (Esteban et al. 2019 Nature Methods, ~5000+ citations) and addresses critical preprocessing gaps. Every TVB user working with fMRI data needs this - it's become an essential standard in the field.

primary_sources.title: fMRIPrep: a robust preprocessing pipeline for functional MRI

gaps_addressed: Quality control and bias field correction

research_targets.rationale: The Allen Brain Atlas is the definitive resource for brain gene expression data across mouse, human, and non-human primates. It's cited thousands of times and provides the anatomical reference atlases essential for TVB modeling. Essential for any user working with strain-specific brain models or genetic data.
search_queries: Allen Brain Atlas Lein 2007 Nature mouse brain expression
Allen Human Brain Atlas Hawrylycz 2012 Nature citation
Allen Brain Atlas API gene expression data

primary_sources.title: Genome-wide atlas of gene expression in the adult mouse brain
primary_sources.authors: Lein ES, Hawrylycz MJ, Ao N, et al.

primary_sources.title: An anatomically comprehensive atlas of the adult human brain transcriptome
primary_sources.authors: Hawrylycz MJ, Lein ES, Guillozet-Bongaarts AL, et al.

primary_sources.title: Allen Brain Atlas: an integrated spatio-temporal portal for exploring the central nervous system
primary_sources.authors: Sunkin SM, Ng L, Lau C, et al.

research_targets.rationale: OpenNeuro is the premier open repository for neuroimaging datasets (fMRI, EEG, MEG). It's the primary source for sharing and discovering public neuroimaging data and is essential for TVB users seeking real brain data for modeling. Strong citation base and growing adoption.
search_queries: OpenNeuro neuroimaging data repository paper citation

primary_sources.title: OpenNeuro: A normative brain imaging database
primary_sources.authors: Gorgolewski K, et al. (with updates and new authors)

primary_sources.title: The OpenNeuro project: A unified repository for neuroimaging datasets

methodology_notes: These 3 targets were selected based on: (1) availability of well-cited primary publications suitable for citation, (2) breadth of impact across TVB user communities (modeling, analysis, data), (3) existing citation chains that can be leveraged. Each addresses distinct gaps but collectively cover the main neuroscience resource categories.
